title: Fewshot Composability Atelier
content:
Summary:
Handy scratchpad for exploring how small exemplar sets (few-shot) behave when we compose, reorder, or hybridize exemplars from different domains/instructions. Goal: find heuristics and lightweight transforms that make exemplar sets robust to mixing (composability) so downstream templates are less brittle in multi-domain product flows.

Quick motivation / context:
- We see a ton of brittleness when swapping in/out exemplars: outputs change style, hallucinate different facts, or flip the interpretation of the instruction.
- Want to enable a single prompt template that can accept exemplar bundles coming from different producers (SRE-run, support-run, user-supplied) without manual curation.
- Tradeoffs: token budget vs robustness, and whether to canonicalize exemplars (rewrite) or to transform the instruction.

Open questions (top-of-mind):
1) Which perturbations of exemplar order matter most? prefix vs interleaved vs grouped-by-intent?
2) Does explicit meta-labeling ("EXEMPLAR: category=doc, tone=concise") increase composability more than rewriting exemplars?
3) Can we cheaply detect when a composed exemplar bundle will cause a style drift and auto-apply a microrewrite?
4) Are some model families (quantized LMs / 7B vs 70B) intrinsically more susceptible to composition failures?

Experiment matrix (rough):
- Variables:
  A: exemplar count: 2, 4, 8
  B: exemplar provenance mix: homogeneous (same domain) vs heterogeneous (2 domains) vs adversarial mix (contradictory instructions)
  C: order: canonical (by time), grouped-by-intent, alternating
  D: meta-tagging: none vs lightweight tags vs explicit instruction header
  E: exemplar rewrite: none vs paraphrase-to-canonical (3 variants)
  F: model: rwd-7b-fp16, rwd-13b-quant, rwd-70b

- Metrics (automated + manual):
  - style-delta: cosine on embedding of generated answer vs target style exemplar embedding
  - factual-drift: number of hallucinated entities (automated via entity list compare)
  - instruction-adherence: rubric score (0-3) measured on 200 seed queries
  - failure-rate: % outputs flagged by heuristics (contradiction, ask-for-clarification, out-of-scope)
  - stability-index: variance of top-k tokens across 10 runs (temperature 0.2, 0.6)

Tiny canonicalization heuristics to test quickly:
- Strip domain-specific headers ("From support ticket #...")
- Normalize date formats and names to placeholders (DATE_1, ORG_1)
- Compress multi-sentence exemplars into 1–2 sentence distilled form (extractive)
- Add a short header before each exemplar: "EXEMPLAR (role=agent, tone=concise)"

Sample template (current):
"You are an assistant that responds concisely. Below are examples labeled with role and intent. Use them as style guides and produce an answer to the final user query.

{EXEMPLARS}

User: {USER_QUERY}
Assistant:"

Example exemplars I used in a quick smoke test (raw):
EX1: "Support: User reported intermittent 502 while uploading. Repro steps: attach file > click upload. Workaround: retry after 10s."
EX2: "Internal runbook: Check ingress LB health, then tail nginx logs on node-3. If 502 persists, rotate worker pool."
EX3: "Marketing blurb: Our upload system handles large files reliably; tips: compress before upload."

Observed weirdness in smoke run:
- When EX3 present, assistant suddenly shifts to promotional tone even though prompt header says "concise".
- Grouped-by-intent reduced tone flip compared to alternating order.
- Adding explicit meta tags (role=) fixed tone 70% of the time but increased hallucination of internal state (e.g., invented node names).

Failure case examples (notes):
- Contradictory guidance: two exemplars recommend different timeouts; model sometimes picks the longer and justifies it with invented data.
- Label bleed: model uses exemplar labels as facts (e.g., treat "Marketing blurb" as canonical product claim).
- Overfitting exemplar details: when exemplar includes numbers ("10s"), outputs tend to anchor to them even when user query context suggests other values.

Lightweight mitigation ideas to prototype:
1) Exemplar redaction for numeric/identifier slots + add a "range suggestion" postscript (e.g., "timeouts often 5–20s").
2) Prepend a single unified instruction that normalizes style and forbids use of exemplar-specific proper nouns.
3) Auto-summarize exemplars into "style vectors" (short label lines: tone=concise; objective=troubleshoot) and provide those instead of full exemplars.
4) Randomized exemplar-order training (for internal fine-tuning) — small corpus of mixed-order exemplars to reduce order sensitivity.

Concrete quick experiments to run this week (low cost):
- Run 200 seed queries using 3 exemplar bundles: homogeneous (EX1+EX2), heterogeneous (EX1+EX3), canonicalized (distill(EX1), distill(EX2), distill(EX3)). Compare instruction-adherence and style-delta at temp 0.2 and 0.6 on rwd-13b-quant.
- Implement a microrewrite: strip identity tokens and replace with placeholders; measure hallucination delta.
- Test adding "role=..." labels vs adding a unified style header only.

Notes to self / heuristics observed in early tests:
- Smaller exemplar counts (2–4) are less brittle if exemplars are curated to avoid contradictory procedural steps.
- Labeling helps tone but sometimes amplifies authority of inaccurate exemplars. Use with caution.
- Canonicalizing numbers into ranges reduces numeric anchoring but may cause loss of specificity (tradeoff).

Ideas for library features (longer term):
- "Composable bundles": metadata + distilled style + provenance score; bundle can be validated by a linter that warns if exemplars conflict.
- Lightweight exemplar linter rules (contradictory steps, numeric ranges, identity leakage).
- A small model-based "alignment check" that flags a composed bundle likely to produce style drift.

Quick TODOs (priority):
- [ ] Build small harness to generate stability-index for 3 models (rwd-7b, -13b, -70b).
- [ ] Write a simple distillation script (extractive summarization) and test automatic distill vs manual distill.
- [ ] Add 200 seed queries and label rubric for instruction-adherence.
- [ ] Sync with Sofia on whether to include marketer exemplars in the public examples library (privacy/policy).

Slack threads / refs: #prompt-lab, #applied-ml-expts
Related tickets: JIRA-ML-481 (cover), CON-1221 (notes page)

Scratchpad mini-playground (3 quick prompt variants to try):
1) No tags, order=EX1,EX2,EX3:
  Prompt: [base header]
  EXEMPLARS:
  - Support: ...
  - Runbook: ...
  - Marketing: ...
  Query: "My upload failed with 502, what do I do?"

2) With meta-tags, grouped-by-intent:
  - "EXEMPLAR (role=support, tone=concise): ..."
  - "EXEMPLAR (role=runbook, tone=procedural): ..."
  - "EXEMPLAR (role=marketing, tone=promotional): ..."

3) Distilled style lines only:
  - "STYLE (tone=concise; objective=troubleshoot)"
  - "STYLE (tone=procedural; objective=diagnose)"
  - "STYLE (tone=promotional; objective=explain)"

If helpful, I'll push a tiny harness to GH and drop the link here. Keep this as my working notes; will iterate into a more formal experiment grid once we have the first batch of results.
